pr_title: R: Full support of lists and structs in R
pr_body:
This adds support for lists of atomic vectors. All elements must be of the same type for this to work. The commits make sense individually, but mostly depend on each other.

ALTREP support can be built on top of that.

Closes #2841.

issue_context.title: R list column support (R is freezing)
issue_context.body:
Hi folks,

Every time I try to write an R dataframe with a column of 'list' type to a DuckDB database, R completely freezes with this message: `Error in duckdb_register(conn, view_name, value): Unsupported column type scan`.

Here is a MWE:
```
.path = tempfile()
con = DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb(), dbdir = .path, read_only = FALSE)

DBI::dbExecute(con, "CREATE TABLE df(id1 INTEGER not null,
                                 id2 VARCHAR not NULL, 
                                 int_list INT[], 
                                 varchar_list VARCHAR[],
                                 primary key (id1, id2))")

df <- tibble::tibble(id1 = as.integer(2), id2 = c("a"),
                     int_list = list(as.integer(1:3)),
                     varchar_list = list(c("a","b")))

DBI::dbWriteTable(con, 'df', df, append=TRUE)
```

(1) Can't DuckDB nested types `integer list column` and `varchar list column` handle R lists?
If not, is there a plan to support it or at least avoid crashing/freezing R?

(2) As a side-question, is there a way to alter DuckDB database to add Primary Keys? This would be important because the current method (declaring primary keys while creating a new table) requires a lot of manual work, like typing all columns of my R dataframe I want to copy to DuckDB (in some cases I have thousands of columns, which would make that impracticable).

Thanks a lot.

#### Environment (please complete the following information):
 - OS: Windows 10 Pro
 - DuckDB Version: 0.3.1-1
 - DuckDB Client: R
comments: It certainly should not crash or freeze in any case.
Yes I can confirm this hangs after the error message. What I meant was that we need to look into it.
This issue is stale because it has been open 90 days with no activity. Remove stale label or comment or this will be closed in 30 days.
I checked now, the issue still remains.

Reprex with a99f5ce0be64bc4ff11fe5257896f88724658b45:

``` r
con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb())

DBI::dbExecute(con, "CREATE TABLE df(id1 INTEGER not null,
                                 id2 VARCHAR not NULL,
                                 int_list INT[],
                                 varchar_list VARCHAR[],
                                 primary key (id1, id2))")
#> [1] 0

df <- tibble::tibble(
  id1 = as.integer(2), id2 = c("a"),
  int_list = list(as.integer(1:3)),
  varchar_list = list(c("a", "b"))
)

DBI::dbWriteTable(con, "df", df, append = TRUE)
#> Error: rapi_execute: Unsupported column type for bind
#> Error: rapi_register_df: Failed to register data frame: std::exception
```

<sup>Created on 2023-08-04 with [reprex v2.0.2](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

It's not as bad as it seems though -- getting nested data from duckdb to R works:

``` r
con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb())

out <- DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT 1 AS a, {'x': 1, 'y': 2, 'z': 3} AS b")
out
#>   a b.x b.y b.z
#> 1 1   1   2   3
tibble::as_tibble(out)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>       a   b$x    $y    $z
#>   <int> <int> <int> <int>
#> 1     1     1     2     3


out <- DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT 1 AS a, [{'x': 1, 'y': 2, 'z': 3}, {'x': 4, 'y': 5, 'z': 6}] AS b")
out
#>   a                b
#> 1 1 1, 4, 2, 5, 3, 6
tibble::as_tibble(out)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>       a b           
#>   <int> <list>      
#> 1     1 <df [2 × 3]>
```

<sup>Created on 2023-08-04 with [reprex v2.0.2](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

If we get to implement this, I think the following tests need to succeed:

```r
test_that("bind plain lists of values", {
  con <- dbConnect(duckdb())
  on.exit(dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE))

  df <- tibble::tibble(a = 1, b = list(2:3))
  expect_equal(rel_to_altrep(rel_from_df(con, df)), df)
})

test_that("bind packed tibble", {
  con <- dbConnect(duckdb())
  on.exit(dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE))

  df <- tibble::tibble(a = 1, b = tibble::tibble(c = 2, d = 3))
  expect_equal(rel_to_altrep(rel_from_df(con, df)), df)
})

test_that("bind nested tibble", {
  con <- dbConnect(duckdb())
  on.exit(dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE))

  df <- tibble::tibble(a = 1, b = list(tibble::tibble(c = 2:3, d = 4:5)))
  expect_equal(rel_to_altrep(rel_from_df(con, df)), df)
})
```

In #8503, also works for nested data frames:

``` r
con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb())

df <- tibble::tibble(
  id1 = as.integer(2), id2 = c("a"),
  int_list = list(as.integer(1:3)),
  varchar_list = list(c("a", "b")),
  packed = tibble::tibble(x = 1, y = 2),
  nested = list(tibble::tibble(u = 1:3, v = 4:6)),
)

DBI::dbWriteTable(con, "df", df, append = TRUE)
tibble::as_tibble(DBI::dbReadTable(con, "df"))
#> # A tibble: 1 × 6
#>     id1 id2   int_list  varchar_list packed$x    $y nested      
#>   <int> <chr> <list>    <list>          <dbl> <dbl> <list>      
#> 1     2 a     <int [3]> <chr [2]>           1     2 <df [3 × 2]>
```

<sup>Created on 2023-08-08 with [reprex v2.0.2](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

review_comments: what does aux_ stand for in this case? Just auxiliary?
Yes, auxiliary information. Can you think of a better name?
maybe `child_Rtypes`? auxiliary feels to broad to me

`aux_` holds the list child type, struct child types and names, or factor levels. It's really a union type, but luckily everything fits into the `child_list_t` . Could be `extra_`, or perhaps `child_types_or_enum_levels_`, or a proper virtual base class with subclasses (but then how do we name that member?).

`BLOB` and `LIST_OF_NULLS` had different logic here https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/8503/files#diff-37ff3203dc9d0866d479ae910101108e08a2bdcf1f93bcf3f357c3be6adc94b3L371 . 
Why are they merged together now?
Will unify the logic at the other location. It's not entirely clear how to treat lists of `NULL`s, but it also doesn't matter because nobody has complained so far.

This was in the original code. I suspect it's more difficult to parse down 12 lines compared to 6 lines.
